gate: On a fresh Kubernetes cluster and in a fresh namespace of an OpenShift cluster, one command installs Away with no rights beyond its namespace. Its three parts answer whether they are well, give their measures and write their lines. The image's signature, the record of its build and the list of what it holds can be checked by anyone. A connection the model doesn't list is refused by the cluster.
note: The repository's layout, the one program with its three parts, the chart, the pipelines

gate: A test program built from Away's own RDP code signs in with a typed name and password on Windows 11, on Windows Server 2025 and on an RDP server on Linux, and saves the desktop's picture. The picture is the machine's screen, pixel for pixel. The owner then says whether the RDP code stays Away's own.
note: The gate of ADR-0001. The pictures matched on all three on 2026-11-14, and the owner said the same day that the RDP code stays Away's own

package: The Windows sign-in, proven without a browser
gate: On a real domain, with a certificate of five minutes that the domain's own authority issued, the test program signs an ordinary account in on a Windows machine with nothing typed, from outside the domain. It reads a file share as that account. An account of the directory's administrators is refused.
note: The proof the first release rests on. Met on 2026-11-15 with the organisation's own authority, which refused an administrator's account, as Away itself did

gate: A person signs in through the organisation's sign-in service and sees the frame on a computer and on a phone, with no token in the page. The sign-in renews itself, and signing out ends it. Every page is used with the keyboard alone and passes the accessibility checks. The pages load nothing from outside. Behind an ingress controller on Kubernetes, Away answers on its address with a certificate of one's own.

package: The register, the rules, and home
gate: With a set of files, every person sees exactly the machines a rule gives them: a test proves it for each person and each machine. A broken file is refused as a whole, its reason shows, and what was in force stays. Every change of the files is a record.

A Windows desktop opens with a typed and with a kept password, takes the window's size and the screen's density, looks as it does at the machine, and meets the targets for the picture. Leaving it running and signing out of the machine both do what they say, and a desktop that was left running is picked up as it was. The record is written before the connection is made, and no connection is made when it can't be written.
note: The first session and the first picture: it brings the session's connection, the session's bar and the records, and is the gate of ADR-0004

gate: Two programs of one Windows machine open in one sign-in, each in windows of its own on Away's ground. The list names every window, brings one to the front, and brings back one that was made small. A window made as large as it gets lies beside the list. On a phone one window shows at a time.

A shell on a real SSH server opens with a typed password, with a kept password and with a kept key, and runs the editors, pagers and monitors of the test list as a terminal of reference does. A machine that shows another identity than the one Away knows is refused. The record is written before the connection is made, and no connection is made when it can't be written. A kept key signs inside the issuer and never leaves it.
note: It opens in the session that package 6 brings

gate: Several shells are open at once, each also in a browser tab of its own. A connection that drops brings a shell back as it was, with what it wrote meanwhile. A session nobody uses warns and then ends. Taking a right away ends the sessions that rested on it within the time its target sets. An administrator sees the sessions that run, ends one, and reads and searches the records, each of which also left Away as a line.

With one line on the machine, a person is in their own account on a shell with nothing typed. The certificate lasts five minutes and names that account alone. An account the issuer never signs in as is refused. Every sign-in is a line of the issuer's own and a record.

A desktop of a Linux machine and of a Mac opens over VNC and meets the targets for the picture: exact once it rests, smooth while a window is dragged, usable on the slow line. Typing arrives in one's own layout, a trackpad scrolls as one is used to, and text is copied both ways. An update of Away tells the people in a session, and their desktops are back by themselves.

On a real domain, from a device that is not in it, a person with an ordinary account opens a Windows desktop with nothing typed, reaches a file share as themselves, and opens the desktop again after it locked. The certificate lasts five minutes and is the organisation's own authority's, which itself refuses one for an account outside the group it allows. An account of the directory's administrators is refused. Nothing of Away's is installed on a Windows machine. With no domain named in the configuration, Away runs as before and shows no authority.
note: With the organisation's own authority. Built on 2026-11-15 ahead of its place, with the issuer the shell as oneself shares; its gate is tried after package 6

gate: With the configuration changed to Away's own authority and nothing else, a person is signed in on a Windows machine as in package 12, on a domain that has no authority of its own: Away's authority has certified its domain controllers too.
note: For a domain that has no authority of its own, proven on a domain that exists for testing

gate: On a phone and on a tablet, in the two browsers most used there, a desktop and a shell are worked by touch: a tap clicks, holding gives the other button, two fingers scroll and zoom, and the keys a phone lacks are there.

package: Status, and the check of the setup
gate: The status page shows each part as it answers. For each kind of mistake in a setup, the check names it in words that say what to do: a wrong client at the sign-in service, a database that can't be reached, a broken file, a machine that isn't there, an authority the domain doesn't trust.

Every quality is measured against its target, and each gap is closed or accepted by the owner. Someone who has not seen Away installs it in the time its target sets. The code that reads what a machine sends has been fuzzed without pause and reviewed by someone outside. Anyone runs the tests against a real server of each protocol with one command.
